draft.title: Advantages of each strategy
card: One parent can reproduce alone, so it does not need to find a mate. It can often produce many offspring quickly.
Offspring differ from each other and from their parents. This variation means some individuals may survive if conditions change.
Asexual reproduction suits a stable environment. Offspring match a parent that already survives there, and a population can grow fast.
Sexual reproduction suits a changing environment. A new disease or a shift in climate is less likely to harm every individual.
draft.remember: Asexual reproduction gives speed without a partner. Sexual reproduction gives variation.

a.q: A lone plant is carried to an empty island and soon spreads across it. Which advantage of asexual reproduction best explains this?
opts: It can reproduce without finding a mate
It produces offspring that differ from the parent
It makes offspring that resist every disease
It combines gametes from two different parents
a.why: One parent can reproduce alone, so a single plant can start a new population. Producing differing offspring is an advantage of sexual reproduction, and asexual offspring match the parent, so they do not gain new resistance.
a.clue: Only one plant arrived on the island.

b.q: A fungus disease spreads through two orchards. Orchard A has trees grown from cuttings of one tree. Orchard B has trees grown from seed. Why is Orchard B more likely to have survivors?
opts: Seed-grown trees vary, so some may resist the disease
Seed-grown trees grow faster, so they outlast the disease
Cutting-grown trees need a partner, so fewer can reproduce
Cutting-grown trees vary, so all of them are harmed equally
b.why: Trees grown from seed come from sexual reproduction, so they differ and some may resist the disease. Trees from cuttings are genetically identical, so a disease that harms one is likely to harm all of them. Speed of growth does not explain survival here.
b.clue: Think about which orchard has trees that differ from each other.

a.best: It can reproduce without finding a mate

b.best: Seed-grown trees vary, so some may resist the disease

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('some may resist'). The other three are flatly stated and plainly flawed, so a student could pick it from tone alone.
